🎯This Lesson’s Objectives▼ Expand
❓
Big Question
Today’s Wonder

Is Robin Hood a hero, an outlaw, or both? Seal seven dispatches from Chapters 18 to 21, then take the king’s own pardon off the pile and see how the evidence reads without it.

🎯
Objectives
By the end of this lesson…
📖Reading: I will seal seven moments from Chapters 18 to 21 green, red, or split, add to my Hero or Outlaw chart, and write my thesis and the best point against it.
✏️Grammar: I will introduce, punctuate, and cite Green’s words in my own writing.
📝Writing: I will revise Quick Write 7, check my Word draft, and turn in Week 7.
📕 You’ll need your copy

Professor Lovelore Literature expert
0:32

Theme
a sentence about what a story says on a topic. A topic is a word, like friendship. A theme says something about it.

🪶 Poetry Corner

The King’s Disguise, and Friendship with Robin Hood
Joseph Ritson, ed., Robin Hood (1832 text)
0:45 AI voice
🖋️ PenTap the line where the king says who he is.
“I am the king, ‘your’ sovereign king, That appears before you all.” When Robin saw that it was he, Strait then he down did fall. Stand up again, then said the king, I’ll thee thy pardon give ; Stand up, my friend, who can contend, When I give leave to live ? [Omitted: 3 stanzas] The king soon did let them understand He had been in the green-wood, And from that day, for evermore, He’d forgiven Robin Hood. Then [when] the people they did hear, And [that] the truth was known, They all did sing, God save the king ! Hang care, the town’s our own !
sovereign: ruler · strait: at once · contend: argue against · forgiven: pardoned · Hang care: forget your worries · the town's our own: the town is ours to enjoy

🍎 At the Board with Professor Lovelore
Three places quotations go wrong
Professor Lovelore At the board
0:36
An AI-generated character and voice.
The dropped quote
“Stand up, my friend” (Ch. 21).→The king tells Robin, “Stand up, my friend” (Ch. 21).
The period
The king tells Robin, “Stand up, my friend.” (Ch. 21)→The king tells Robin, “Stand up, my friend” (Ch. 21).
The marks
The king will pardon all here present (Ch. 21).→The king will pardon “all here present” (Ch. 21).

Three lenses for your essay
  1. Quotes. Every quotation is marked. One that stands alone, or has no chapter citation, is flagged.
  2. Explain. The sentence after each quotation is checked for what the quotation shows.
  3. Present tense. Past and present verbs are marked. A sentence that mixes them is flagged.
